During the holidays, Bassam worked for Uncle Zakariyya, the watch repairer in the old market.

He loved the sound of all the clocks on the wall, ticking together as if they were talking.

Uncle Zakariyya worked slowly. He would open a watch, clean every piece inside it, and tighten every tiny screw until it was firm. Then he would listen to it for a long time before closing it.

Bassam would say to himself, "Why does he take so long?"

One day Uncle Zakariyya went out to pray, and a man came in with a watch that had stopped. He said, "I need it in an hour — I'm travelling."

Bassam said, "I'll fix it for you."

Bassam opened it quickly and moved its hands, and they turned. So he closed it without tightening the tiny screw inside it, and said, "Done!"

The man took it happily and left.

When Uncle Zakariyya came back, he looked at the table and saw the tiny screw lying on it.

He said, "Where's the watch this came out of, Bassam?"

In the evening the man came back angry, holding the watch, which had stopped. He said, "It stopped on the way, and I nearly missed my train!"

Bassam's face turned red, and he lowered his head.

Uncle Zakariyya apologised to the man and fixed the watch slowly in front of him, and did not charge him anything.

Then, after the man had gone, he said to Bassam, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah loves that when one of you does a job, he does it well.'"

Then he said, "Quick, unfinished work has to be done twice. Work done well only has to be done once."

Bassam said, "Teach me to work like you."

So Bassam began opening the watches slowly, counting their pieces, tightening every screw, and listening to them before closing them.

It took him time — but not one of the watches he fixed ever came back to him.

A month later, the same man came back with his father's old watch and said, "I want Bassam to fix it."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah loves that when one of you does a job, he does it well."

📖 Narrated by Al-Bayhaqi. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
